messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: GPU pool 'inference-prod' is reporting sustained queue growth > 90% for 18m, HPA not scaling. Autoscaler health: DEGRADED. Prometheus adapter lagging behind by ~6m. Trigger: GPU-queue-throttle-alert-1763337777.
Emma (oncall): acked. I'm on it, taking incident lead. Starting quick triage. Can someone post current queue size and pod count?
Raj (sre): queue ~12k requests (avg arrival 220r/s) across three nodepools. inference-prod pods = 12, avg util ~98%. HPA metrics show stable but outdated since adapter scrape delay. Prom-adapter logs show repeated 429s to metrics-api (rate limit) and batching backlog.
Liam (platform): quota-wise we have 8 spare GPUs in region-us-west; but autoscaler has been stuck due to metrics lag. Manual scale is possible but we should avoid blasting capacity if adapter still blocked.
Emma (oncall): Sophia, any customer-facing hits yet?
Sophia (customer-success): We've received 2 tickets and a handful of errors from key accounts in the last 10m — errors are 502/504 and slow responses. Raise to P1 for CS. Customers flagged inference timeouts on /v1/generate.
Maya (eng-sre): I'm looking at prometheus-adapter. It has a backlog of ~1.2M custom metric samples in the write queue; the backfill job crashed earlier with OOM. Logs snippet:
```
ERROR prometheus-adapter: write failed: context deadline exceeded
panic: runtime: out of memory
```
Maya (eng-sre): adapter restart helps but backfill will keep spamming until we fix ingestion. Recommend pausing low-priority jobs and cleaning the backlog.
Raj (sre): mitigation plan: 1) Pause non-essential inference queues (batch/low-pri) via rate-limit gate. 2) Restart prometheus-adapter with increased memory, disable backfill for 10m. 3) Manually scale inference-prod by +4 GPUs to soak current backlog. 4) Re-route critical customers to dedicated pool fallback.
Liam (platform): I'll open an emergency request to add burst GPUs to the cluster and run `kubectl scale --replicas=16 deploy/inference-prod -n inference` if approved. Also can temporarily open fallback routing at the edge to send <10% traffic to model-fallback-1.
Emma (oncall): Execute step 1 now — Maya can you throttle batch queue?
Maya (eng-sre): throttling gate applied to queue 'batch-low' and 'async-training'. That should reduce new arrivals by ~35%.
Maya (eng-sre): Restarting prometheus-adapter now with mem limit 1.5Gi -> 3Gi, flags: `--disable-backfill` and `--scrape-interval=15s`.
ops-bot: deploy/prometheus-adapter restart initiated by Maya. CI job 4523.
Maya (eng-sre): Adapter back up, but initial logs show 429s are gone. Writing backlog to temporary S3 archive to be pruned. Running cleanup script: `scripts/adapter/cleanup_backlog.sh --archive s3://redwood-adapter-backlog/1763337777`
Raj (sre): Manual scale submitted. Approval from platform: granted. Running `kubectl scale deploy/inference-prod --replicas=16 -n inference`.
ops-bot: scale action accepted, cluster API returning 4 new pods scheduled.
Liam (platform): Note: autoscaler constraints will prevent further auto-scaling until adapter reports metrics. Put an explicit annotation to bypass HPA lock for 20m: `redwood.io/hpa-bypass=true` (temporary). I'll apply it.
Emma (oncall): Re-route in progress: set routing rule to send traffic to model-fallback-1 for customers with tag `cs-critical` (10%) and increase timeouts to 90s.
Sophia (customer-success): Confirmed one customer already moved to fallback and latency for them returned to normal. CS pushing updates to affected accounts. :thumbsup:
Maya (eng-sre): Cleanup job finished archive size ~1.1GB, removed 1.2M samples from adapter queue. Prom-adapter now reporting fresh metrics. HPA metric lag reduced to <20s.
Raj (sre): Observed immediate effect: HPA sees increased desired replicas and will start scaling automatically. Current target increased to 18, pods spinning up. Queue drained from 12k -> 4k in 9m. Throttling applied to batch queues helped.
Emma (oncall): Good. Customer error rate dropping from 6% -> 0.8% over 12m. Continue to monitor but looks like live mitigations worked.
Liam (platform): Removing `hpa-bypass` annotation now that adapter is healthy to restore normal control.
Emma (oncall): Handing off to Raj for stabilization and RCA ownership. Raj, your checklist: keep throttles in place for 30m, monitor HPA/adapter for 1h, collect prometheus-adapter logs & heap profile, create post-incident ticket with ETA for permanent backpressure fix.
Raj (sre): Taking over. Will file incident: INC-1763337777 and start RCA. Immediate action items: 1) autoscaler should tolerate adapter lag for short windows — propose adding short-lived metrics fallback that uses node-level GPU queue heuristic. 2) introduce graceful backpressure on producers. 3) set up alert to detect prometheus-adapter backlog >100k samples.
Sophia (customer-success): I'll coordinate CS comms and send interim note to affected customers with ETA for RCA and mitigation summary.
ops-bot: Incident resolved? status=monitoring, duration=36m, impact=partial (some requests degraded), mitigation=throttled batch + adapter restart + manual scale + fallback routing.
Emma (oncall): Closing page; moving to postmortem. Thanks team — big props for quick coordination. :clap:
Raj (sre): Adding link to logs and heap profile in the postmortem ticket. Will propose follow-ups in the next 24h.
Sophia (customer-success): Marking customers as notified.
incident-bot: Incident thread archived after handoff to RCA owner.
__notes: this document is a synthetic Slack thread for incident coordination: GPU capacity exhaustion caused by metrics pipeline lag causing delayed autoscaling. Includes bot messages, oncall handoff, mitigation steps, manual scaling, and customer impact notes.
